# Four-Factor Interaction Effects: Does Combining All Factors Superadditively Increase Offensive Behavior?

**Problem:** Irregular 2026 lists four contributing factors individually. Whether the factors interact (i.e., combining all four produces more than the sum of individual effects) has not been studied.

**Direction:** Design a full factorial experiment (2^4 = 16 conditions) varying each factor on/off. Run 30 trials per condition. Measure offensive action rate in each condition. Use ANOVA with interaction terms to test for superadditive interactions.

**Why it matters:** If the factors interact superadditively, organizations cannot simply control one factor and assume safety. If they are independent, focused controls are sufficient. This distinction has major implications for deployment policy.

**Relevant context:** Irregular 2026 four-factor model; standard factorial experimental design from psychology/medicine.
